title: Late Provisioning on Web Hosting Plans: Compensation Basis by Length of Delay
content:
# Compensation basis by length of delay

The compensation basis of the late-provisioning goodwill figure depends on how long the provisioning was late, counted as the days from the plan's order date to its activation date.

| Days the late provisioning lasted | Compensation basis of the late-provisioning goodwill figure |
|---|---|
| 7 or more | the plan's monthly term value for each started week of those days |
| 3 or more but fewer than 7 | one monthly term value |
| fewer than 3 | the plan's daily term value times those days |

The plan's monthly term value is the plan's initial-term charge divided by the plan's term length in months. A started week counts in full: 7 days are one started week, 8 to 14 days are two, 15 days are three.

## Illustrations (hypothetical figures)

A 24-month plan whose initial-term charge was $311.76 has a monthly term value of $311.76 divided by 24, which is $12.99.

- Activated 10 days after its order date: two started weeks, a basis of $12.99 times 2, $25.98.
- Activated 5 days after its order date: one monthly term value, $12.99.
- Activated 7 days after its order date: one started week, $12.99.
- Activated 6 days after its order date: one monthly term value, $12.99, since 6 is fewer than 7.

*Applies to: Harborline Customer Accounts, for plans held under Web Hosting Plans*
